subject: Capacity landing playbook & commitment cadence
messages:
From: Claudia Reyes <claudia@opushealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity landing playbook & commitment cadence

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed internally, OpusHealth is ready to move from proof-of-concept into a small production footprint, but procurement needs a mutual action plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to committed capacity. High level asks below so we can align on timeline and internal approvals: 

- Evaluation window: 6 weeks starting Jan 4. Key gate is quality regression <1% on our PR prompt set.
- Desired go-live target: March 1 (soft), April 1 (hard).
- Preferred deployment: Private (VPC) with a Dedicated pool for latency-sensitive endpoints; we need explicit lead times for both Dedicated reservation and Private on-prem onboarding.
- Rough workload: initially 40 concurrent active users with median prompt length ~500 tokens; burst headroom up to 4x for peak clinic hours.

From procurement: we need a MAP with dates, acceptance gates, and proposed GPU sizing so legal can align on contract terms and finance can estimate commit levels. Can you share a compact playbook with 2–3 sizing options and the expected procurement lead times (dedicated GPU tranche availability, on-prem hardware delivery estimates)?

Attaching a one-pager with our SLA expectations and a sketch of traffic profile.

Attachments: opus_map_v1.xlsx (Opus internal runbook), provisioning_sketch.png

Best,
Claudia
Head of Platform Engineering
OpusHealth
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claudia Reyes <claudia@opushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity landing playbook & commitment cadence

Claudia —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level reply and proposed MAP draft below. I added Marissa, Ben and Irene to scope sizing, procurement cadence, and security handoffs.

Draft MAP (summary):
- Week 0 (Jan 4): Onboard evaluation tenants to a shared staging Dedicated pool; Redwood provides baseline perf profile and KV caching config.
- Week 2: Mid-eval checkpoint — QA/regression run, perf numbers, decide tranche sizing.
- Week 4: Final eval gate — quality/regression checks + scale test to 2x baseline.
- Week 6 (Feb 15): MAP sign-off for primary tranche reservation and contract signature window.
- Operational cutover target: staged traffic to Private Dedicated pool starting Mar 1; full redirect Apr 1.

Lead times (ballpark, subject to final PO):
- Redwood Dedicated reservation (cloud host): 3–5 business days to provision capacity once tranche is agreed and PO issued.
- Dedicated capacity cold-start (if custom HW requested): 4–6 weeks (procurement + provisioning).
- Private/VPC control-plane onboarding: 2–3 weeks for control plane + 1–3 weeks for network and KMS integration (customer dependent).
- On-prem hardware delivery (if chosen): 8–12 weeks typical for H100-class racks — can be accelerated via preferred partners with additional cost.

I'll circulate a concise MAP workbook with 3 sizing options (Conservative / Recommended / Aggressive) and a suggested cadence for procurement sign-off. Can we set a 30-minute sync on Friday to walk the options with procurement and SRE?

On Fri 18:00 PT works for me; please confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: redwood_capacity_SLA_v2.pdf

Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity landing playbook & commitment cadence (internal)

Folks —

Quick internal sizing run based on Claudia's traffic sketch and our perf baselines. Assumptions: model ~Redwood-7B-LLM (quantized), median response 500 tokens, avg RPS per active user 0.12, baseline KV cache hit 22% for prompts. Latency SLO (p95) < 250ms.

Sizing options (initial tranche):
1) Conservative (pilot): 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (shared 1:8 continuous batching) — supports ~30 active users at target latency, cost-efficient, fast to provision (3–5 business days).
2) Recommended (production-light): 8 x A100/H100-similar GPUs (lower batch ratio, reserved slots) — supports ~60 active users with headroom for 2x bursts, expected to meet p95 SLO with KV caching. Lead time: immediate reservation (cloud) or 4–6 weeks if custom node spec.
3) Aggressive (dedicated): 16 x H100-class GPUs (dedicated pool) —  supports >150 active users, allowed sustained throughput for batch workloads; procurement lead for custom on-prem racks ~8–12 weeks.

Procurement cadence suggestion:
- Week 0: start evaluation on Conservative tranche (cloud dedicated).
- Week 2: scale to Recommended tranche if mid-eval perf looks good (we can provision additional GPUs in 3–5 business days cloud-side).
- Week 4–6: finalize contract for primary tranche (Recommended or Aggressive) with staggered tranches: 50% immediate reserved, 50% scheduled as 90-day option.

Network/KMS notes for Private: need a 2-week window to validate KMS keys + sec group rules in staging. If they want on-prem racks, add the 8–12 week hardware lead.

I can build the workbook with projected token costs, expected monthly run-rate per tranche, and a short risk matrix (SOC2 gating, audit log retention).

Marissa
VP, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claudia Reyes <claudia@opushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity landing playbook & commitment cadence

Claudia —

Thanks — attached is the concise MAP workbook (opus_map_v1.xlsx updated) with the three sizing options Marissa outlined, a recommended cadence, and procurement-friendly language for the PO and SLA windows. Key bullets: 

- We propose starting evaluation Jan 4 on the Conservative tranche (cloud Dedicated 4x A10-equivalent).
- Contingency: scale to Recommended (8x A100/H100-equivalent) mid-eval; cloud-side provisioning typically 3–5 business days once tranche is agreed.
- For Private control-plane + VPC: expect 2–3 weeks for control plane and KMS; network testing to be scheduled during weeks 1–2 of the eval.
- If Opus elects on-prem racks, Redwood can provide vendor list and accelerated procurement path (8–12 week delivery).

Next steps:
1) Confirm the Jan 4 start date and stakeholders for weekly MAP checkpoint (clause to be included in workbook).
2) Can procurement issue an indicative PO for the initial tranche by Feb 15 to lock pricing and capacity? We recommend a two-tranche contract: 50% immediate reservation + 50% optional reserve to be exercised within 90 days.

I'll open a HubSpot deal note and attach the workbook (link below). If that all looks good I suggest we lock in a 30-min touchpoint tomorrow at 11:00 PT to walk the playbook with procurement and SRE.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/OPUS-3251
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_OPUS_MAP

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_capacity_SLA_v2.pdf, opus_map_v1.xlsx
